name: GigaFound Content Engine
author: meureii63

sections.description:
GigaFound helps small businesses prepare useful content from their business information and connected Google Search Console data. Research and content creation run in GigaFound, keeping your WordPress website responsive.

The everyday workflow is simple:

  • Connect your GigaFound account and Google Search Console.
  • Choose Start Next Article.
  • Review the finished draft in the normal WordPress editor.
  • Edit and publish it yourself.
  • Review and approve the proposed finishing improvements together.

Articles, progress and connections are shared with your GigaFound workspace. Optional illustrations follow your website preferences. GigaFound does not promise rankings, traffic or business results.

Hosted service and 14-day trial

This is a free, GPL-licensed connector to the GigaFound hosted service. A GigaFound account is required for hosted research, content creation, analysis and approved finishing work. New eligible accounts receive a 14-day service trial after confirming their email, with no payment card required. Trial usage allowances apply. After the trial, choose and confirm a recurring paid plan to continue hosted production. There is no automatic charge merely because a trial ends.

The plugin itself does not expire. Existing WordPress articles, the normal WordPress editor and your account/billing access remain available. Uninstalling, reconnecting or adding another website does not start a second trial. See https://gigafound.com/pricing/ for current plans and https://gigafound.com/terms/ for service terms.

Privacy and external services

Installing or activating the plugin does not send website data to GigaFound. You initiate connection using Connect GigaFound and approve the website connection in your account.

After connection, the plugin communicates over HTTPS with https://app.gigafound.com for authenticated website ownership, shared workflow status, preferences, publication notices, drafts and specifically approved changes. GigaFound can read website posts and pages (including drafts/private/scheduled content for duplicate prevention), their metadata, categories, tags, links and media descriptions. Article text, approved media and metadata are transferred when preparing drafts or applying approved finishing changes. Connection uses a dedicated limited WordPress service user and revocable application password; it does not grant permission to install plugins or administer unrelated users. Connection credentials are stored privately. Disconnect the dashboard in GigaFound Settings to revoke its dashboard grant; any separately configured website publishing connection must also be removed in your GigaFound account if desired.

Google Search Console is optional to connect but required for the automatic search-informed article workflow. Its OAuth consent happens in your browser through GigaFound. Google grants and AI-provider keys remain in the GigaFound backend, not in WordPress. GigaFound uses authorized Google search data and its configured AI providers for hosted research, writing, independent review and optional images. The plugin does not connect directly to Google or AI-provider APIs. See https://gigafound.com/privacy/ for data handling and subprocessors, and https://gigafound.com/terms/ for terms.

No unrelated tracking, public-site advertising, executable code downloads or automatic customer publication is included. You remain responsible for reviewing content and confirming publication.

Compatibility

A public HTTPS WordPress website on one server, PHP 8.2+, application-password support, OpenSSL and InnoDB posts/options storage are required. Other website systems and multi-server WordPress hosting are not supported. A managed private operation-lock directory is prepared outside your public website with a bounded pool of lock files and guarded uninstall cleanup; hosts may configure GIGAFOUND_OPERATION_LOCK_DIR when necessary. Writes stop safely if private locking is unavailable. Yoast SEO must be installed and active to save article search and sharing information. WordPress identifies this plugin dependency during installation. No ranking or green-score guarantee is made.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, open Plugins, then Add New Plugin, and find GigaFound Content Engine once its WordPress.org listing is approved.
  2. Choose Install Now, then Activate. If WordPress prompts for Yoast SEO, install and activate that dependency first.
  3. Open GigaFound in your WordPress dashboard and choose Connect GigaFound.
  4. Sign in or create your account, confirm your email and secure your account.
  5. Approve your website connection. Return to WordPress and choose Check connection. If the connection expires during account setup, choose Connect GigaFound again; your trial is not restarted.
  6. Connect Google Search Console in Settings, confirm your business details, and select your website if needed.
  7. Start Next Article when setup and the hosted workflow are available.

For a release supplied directly by GigaFound, Upload Plugin also accepts the provided ZIP. No API keys or normal WordPress login passwords need to be pasted into this plugin.
sections.faq:
Will GigaFound publish without my review?

No. Drafts are reviewed and published in WordPress by you. Finishing changes require your approval of the exact proposed changes.

What happens after the trial?

Select a paid plan in your GigaFound account to continue hosted content production. Existing saved articles are not deleted or hidden, and no payment is taken without subscription confirmation.

Does connecting Google mean data is already available?

No. The dashboard distinguishes connection, website selection, completed imports and available search information. Missing information is not reported as zero traffic.

What if my website does not use WordPress?

This plugin is for supported WordPress websites. It does not provide publishing for Payload, Wix or other systems.
sections.changelog:
0.9.0

Service-trial and plan guidance, account-setup continuation, source-capture improvements and directory documentation. Automatic article drafting, native WordPress review and publication, and verified finishing approval. Hosted availability depends on site setup and an active service trial or plan. WordPress.org approval is required for directory installation.

0.8.0

Native dashboard, secure account pairing and queued publication notices.

0.6.0

Guarded publishing and editing, metadata, media and result recovery.

Connection permissions

Only a signed-in WordPress administrator can initiate pairing, protected by a WordPress nonce. Pairing locally creates a dedicated revocable content-service identity. Its role can read, edit and publish posts/pages and upload media; it cannot manage users, plugins, themes, code or site settings. GigaFound has no remote endpoint for creating users or changing roles. The credentials sent during pairing belong only to that content identity, not the administrator. Normal publication and finishing approvals remain required. Disconnect/revocation and tenant-specific credential storage are documented above.

0.9.1

Directory review corrections: longer declaration and new-operation prefixes with legacy receipt compatibility, consistent WordPress minimum version, managed bounded private locks and guarded cleanup, and prepared WordPress database queries that preserve atomic reservation and prohibit reconnect/replay. Customer workflow, existing grants and article approvals are preserved.

0.9.2

Fix a fatal error on normal WordPress startup by preparing private operation locks only after WordPress loads its pluggable authentication functions. Existing connections, private locking safeguards and publishing approvals are unchanged.
